note: Machine form of VOICE-LAWS.md. regex laws run free/offline; judge laws need --judge. appliesTo: 'finding' = headline+narrative+recommendation per finding; 'summary' = report summary; 'all' = both.

checks.explain: Indicts the owner's work — the canonical banned construction

checks.question: Would the person who BUILT the element under critique feel accused or informed? The text must critique moments/elements and frame findings as recoverable opportunity, never as the owner doing a bad job, and must contain no wit at the site's expense. Does this text comply?

Does the narrative OPEN by granting the strongest honest reason the design might be intentional (a real cost or constraint — the steelman), before showing where that trade-off leaks value? An opening that goes straight to the problem fails.

checks.explain: Synthesized-quote device or quote-led narrative in customer-facing copy

checks.question: Does the customer-facing narrative lead with, or lean on, a simulated/synthesized customer quote or imagined customer inner monologue? (Quotes belong only in evidence refs.) Answer compliant only if no such device appears in the narrative.

checks.pattern: trust break|expectation break|credibility leak|friction at intent|commitment mismatch|buried value|confidence gap|coherence break
checks.explain: Internal taxonomy label in customer-facing copy

checks.question: Is every consequence stated in business terms (abandonment, discounted claims, lost sales, trust spent) rather than speculated user emotions ('users might feel confused')?

checks.explain: Narrative contains no number at all — likely unlocated/uncounted (heuristic; judge grades fully)

checks.question: Does every substantive claim carry a count and a location ('14 of 16 products', 'step 4 of your checkout')? Adjectives arriving without a number or location fail.

checks.explain: A percentage claimed while the finding's research field is null — free-recalled statistic

checks.question: IF the text makes any claim about a competitor: is it attributed to a verifiable observation from this run (named competitor, what was seen, link/screenshot reference) AND does it actually contrast with the site under review? A competitor claim that is unverified, vague, or shows the competitor doing the same thing fails. If no competitor is mentioned, answer compliant.

checks.explain: Score or dev-speak unit in customer-facing copy
Report has no strengths — praise is what makes critique credible (zero findings reports exempt)

checks.question: Are the listed strengths specific and evidenced ('96% true-to-size shown at the size picker') rather than generic ('clean design', 'good navigation')?
